name: Rings scUSD
oneLiner: scUSD is Rings' wrapper minted from supported stablecoins routed through Veda BoringVault DeFi strategies; yield is activated by staking into stkscUSD.
collateral: Stablecoin deposits routed through Trevee (formerly Rings) / Veda BoringVault infrastructure into curated DeFi lending strategies (e.g. Aave, Morpho); supported collateral includes USDC, USDT, DAI, GHO, and Sonic USDC.e
pegMechanism: Users deposit supported stablecoins to mint scUSD and redeem scAssets after a documented cooldown period; yield is primarily activated by staking scUSD into stkscUSD rather than by holding liquid scUSD itself.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: 2026-07-30 re-review of both material deployments (Ethereum block 25648302, Sonic block 76778912). scUSD is the immutable Veda BoringVault share token at 0xd3dce716f3ef535c5ff8d041c1a41c3bd89b97ae on Ethereum and Sonic (owner()=0; authority=RolesAuthority 0x7D5f6108e23c0CB2cfD744E5c46f1aAfFc30A348). transfer/transferFrom call BeforeTransferHook; on both chains hook() returns the LayerZeroTeller 0x358CFACf00d0B4634849821BB3d1965b472c776a. That Teller bytecode and the public TellerWithMultiAssetSupport source expose denyAll/denyFrom/denyTo/denyOperator (requiresAuth) and beforeTransfer(from,to,operator), which reverts TransferDenied for deny-listed parties and SharesAreLocked during any share-lock window. shareLockPeriod()=0 and isPaused()=false at observation; deny calls from unprivileged callers revert UNAUTHORIZED, so activation is gated by RolesAuthority grants under chain-specific 4/6 Veda/Paladin Safe + one-day TimelockController paths documented in mintAuthority. Failure domain: Veda/Paladin RolesAuthority+Teller deny surface on each chain, plus LayerZero share routing. Upstream USDC/USDT/DAI/GHO freeze exposure remains via reserves and is not the token-level control path. Direct holder freeze/blacklistability is therefore true, not merely possible.

mintAuthority.summary: scUSD is a Veda BoringVault receipt token on Ethereum and Sonic. Each immutable vault authorizes the same-address LayerZeroTeller, while a chain-specific 4/6 Veda/Paladin Safe controls role grants through a one-day TimelockController and RolesAuthority.

controls.label: Ethereum Veda/Paladin governance Safe (4/6)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25526164, the 4/6 Safe was the TimelockController proposer; the one-day Timelock owned the RolesAuthority that administers BoringVault capabilities. Safe reads returned six owners, no enabled modules, and zero guard and module guard.

controls.label: Ethereum scUSD LayerZeroTeller
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25526164, current RolesAuthority capability reads identified this LayerZeroTeller as the sole external contract authorized to enter the BoringVault and mint scUSD shares against supported deposits and the configured exchange rate.

controls.label: Sonic Veda/Paladin governance Safe (4/6)
controls.evidence: At Sonic block 75897805, the 4/6 Safe was the TimelockController proposer; the one-day Timelock owned the RolesAuthority that administers BoringVault capabilities. Safe reads returned the same six owners as Ethereum, no enabled modules, and zero guard and module guard.

controls.capDescription: Can update the Accountant exchange rate within the configured 0.5% per-update bounds and six-hour minimum interval; this is not a hard mint cap.

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 25526164 and Sonic block 75897805, current RolesAuthority capabilities and complete role histories resolved the sole direct BoringVault enter caller, both chain-specific governance Safes, and all four Accountant role-11 rate updater Safes. Safe thresholds, owners, modules, guards, fallback handlers, and master copies were read onchain. The deployed BoringVault and LayerZeroTeller contracts are immutable non-proxy deployments.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: scUSD is reviewed as a Sonic/Ethereum Rings asset whose architecture includes cross-chain components: underlying capital is bridged through the Sonic bridge and vault shares can be bridged through LayerZero. Because holder-facing supply can depend on bridge/vault-share routing, Pharos scores the route as external lock/mint.
